title: Johannes Høsflot Klæbo sets Winter Olympic gold record as Norway wins cross-country relay
content:
TESERO, Italy — Johannes Høsflot Klæbo broke the all-time Winter Olympics gold medal record on Sunday with his ninth career gold as Norway won the men’s cross-country skiing team relay off a dominant performance from Klæbo, Emil Iversen, Martin Løwstrøm Nyenget and Einar Hedegart.

France, led by two-time silver medalist Mathis Desloges, took second, and Italy finished third for its first cross-country skiing medal of its home games. Coming down to the final lap, team veteran Federico Pellegrino beat out Finland in a close battle for the podium.

“It was a fantastic race, great to be able to give this gold medal to Norway,” Klæbo said in Norwegian after the race. “The other guys made it so possible and easy for me. It’s a team result and everyone, so many people involved, and I want to share the victory with all of them.”

It’s an impressive showing from Norway, which also won the women’s team relay on Saturday with an upset over Sweden.

Already the most decorated men’s cross-country skier of all time, Klæbo has now won all four golds on offer so far at these Games as he looks for a sweep. With his nine Olympic golds, he passes fellow Norwegian biathlete Ole Einar Bjørndalen and cross-country skiers Bjørn Dæhlie and Marit Bjørgen for most all-time.

Nyenget and Hedegart won their second medals of the Games after picking up bronze in the skiathlon and 10k, respectively.

The Norwegian team built Klæbo a 12.2-second lead heading into the final leg, which he stretched to 22.2 seconds over France by the end, crossing the finish at a cruising pace into the arms of his teammates waiting with a Norwegian flag.

France’s Victor Lovera crossed next, waving a French flag, for his country’s third silver in cross-country skiing at the Games.

The real battle, however, came for bronze, with Pellegrino and Finland’s Niko Anttola neck and neck for most of the final lap. While Norwegian fans far outnumbered anyone else in the stands on Sunday, local volunteers lined up along the barricade lining the final stretch, tension palpable, as Pellegrino made his move on Anttola to clinch third.

The veteran of an otherwise young team, Pellegrino, 35, was Italy’s flag bearer to kick off the Games. Already a two-time silver medalist, the bronze marks Pellegrino’s third Olympic medal, but his first at home.

“It is something that I was dreaming since long time, but I think two years ago, when I started to think about home Olympics, and I see the teammates increasing their level, the dream became a goal, and today we achieved it,” Pellegrino said. “It’s maybe the thing that I’m most proud of in my career.”

Next up is the team sprint on Wednesday, followed by the 50k on Saturday. Klæbo will enter as the favorite, as he has throughout the entire Games. If he wins those two competitions, he would be the first man to sweep all six cross-country skiing events at the Olympics.
